text:
sasha: fyi seeing a recurring latency tail on prod when long-context sessions (>6k tokens) hit sustained token rates. KV reuse percent drops from ~92% -> 48% and paging spikes.
sasha: reproduces in canary with skewed batch sizes (mix of 1-token and 512-token requests). Not seeing OOMs, just big 50-200ms p99 blips per request.
ryan: ugh that sounds like cache fragmentation + eviction churn. any flamegraphs / pprof?
sasha: pushed a short profile to traces: https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/0xabc123 (session: session-fall-through). Key points below:

```
- kv_lookup_total: 1.2M
- kv_reuse_hits: 571k (47.6%)
- pager_evictions: 12.3k
- avg_reinsert_latency: 0.9ms -> 3.8ms during spike
- cpu: runtime-thread busy in kv_reinsert_hotpath
- gpu kernels: kernel selection flip from fast-atten->fallback for small sequences
```

maria: interesting that kernel flip shows up. Could be our batching heuristic sending tiny/huge mixed batches which forces a conservative kernel.

dan: do we have a timeline of FIFO vs LRU decisions? I remember we recently toggled the prob-evict hysteresis.
ryan: yes, the new hysteresis reduces aggressive reuse eviction but under bursty mixed batches it seems to cause a reinsert cascade: entries evicted by FIFO, then reinserted immediately when the long request hits -> fragmentation.

oliver: quick question — are these eviction events concurrent across threads or single-threaded pager? concurrency profile would change latencies a lot.
sasha: concurrent; pager worker pool size is 3 on those hosts. I can repro with a stress test that hits multiple lanes.

prod-oncall: rolling a small tweak to decrease pager concurrency from 3->1 on one canary to see if that reduces tail. deploy-bot: started rollout 4759991200 -> canary hosts.

maria: alternative mitigation: bump KV reuse threshold for long-lived sessions so we avoid evicting entries whose age < 10s; also try grouping batches by seq len to avoid kernel flip.
dan: sounds good. we should also add a telemetry counter for "kernel_flip_due_to_batch_mix" so we can correlate with latency spikes.

ryan: for quick fix I propose: 1) revert the hysteresis tweak (restore old eviction aggressiveness) 2) enable batching-window alignment (30ms) to coalesce similar seq lengths 3) telemetry + alert.

sasha: i'll run the stress job with these changes and attach results.

sasha: early results on canary: tail improved p99 from 380ms -> 150ms after grouping batches and reducing pager concurrency. reuse went up to ~88%.

dan: great. open a follow-up PR to make batching-window and pager-concurrency configurable per pool, add tests for mixed-size workloads.

maria: filing followup doc + perf regression ticket.

sasha: thanks all :thumbsup:
